approachQuestion.prompt:
Distinct Shipment Batch

An array `scores` gives signed scores of shipments in order. Return the greatest sum of a contiguous batch of exactly k shipments whose identifiers are all distinct, using parallel array `ids`. Return null if no eligible batch exists; negative answers are valid.

Limits and assumptions:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; ids.length = scores.length = n; 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
• Each id is a signed 32-bit integer; -10^6 ≤ scores[i] ≤ 10^6. Sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Neither array may be changed.

Examples:
1. ids = [1,1,2,3], scores = [9,8,-2,4], k = 3 → 10, from indices 1 through 3.
2. ids = [1,1], scores = [-2,-3], k = 2 → null.
3. ids = [1,2], scores = [-5,-2], k = 2 → -7.

Choose one approach.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; ids.length = scores.length = n; 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Each id is a signed 32-bit integer; -10^6 ≤ scores[i] ≤ 10^6. Sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Neither array may be changed.

options.text: Move a length-k window, maintaining its score sum and a frequency table of identifiers, deleting zero counts. Consider its sum exactly when the table has k keys; initialize best as absent.
options.feedback: A window of k entries has all distinct identifiers exactly when it has k distinct keys. An absent best distinguishes no candidate from a negative valid sum.

options.text: For each length-k batch, scan its entries into a fresh set, sum its scores, and consider the sum if the set size is k. Keep best absent until a valid batch appears.
options.feedback: The validity and negative-result handling are correct, but adjacent batches repeatedly rebuild equivalent state.

options.text: Use rolling sum and exact frequency validity, but initialize best=0 and return it even if every eligible batch has a negative sum.
options.feedback: For ids [1,2], scores [-5,-2], k=2 the required answer is -7, not zero.

options.text: Within each length-k batch, ignore later shipments with a repeated identifier and sum only the first occurrence of each identifier. Return the greatest such sum.
options.feedback: Every shipment in the selected batch must be eligible. ids [1,1], scores [2,3], k=2 has no valid batch, not a reduced sum of two.

feedback.reason: A full k-window is eligible only when the map has k distinct keys.
details: Initialize counts and sum for the first k shipments. For each full window, compare its sum against an optional best only if its count table has k keys. Slide by decrementing the outgoing identifier, deleting zero counts, adding the incoming identifier, and replacing the score contribution. Return null if best stays absent.

A full k-window is eligible only when the map has k distinct keys. Remove zero-frequency keys so map size means active distinct count. Use an absent best state: zero would incorrectly beat every valid negative score.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Maintain eligibility and score together” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair under the stated expected hashing model.
constraints: Assume expected constant-time hash lookup, update and delete, including amortized resizing and allocated capacity.
Arithmetic and random access take unit cost. Input and scalar output are excluded; no segments are copied. The iterative call stack is constant.

options.text: Expected O(n) time, O(k) auxiliary space
Expected O(nk) time, O(k) auxiliary space
Expected O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space
Expected O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Maintain one k-window sum and expected-cost frequency table.
details: Every shipment enters and leaves at most once, and the table has at most k active identifiers. Expected hash work is linear, including resizing, while auxiliary space is O(k). Keeping a separate absent state preserves valid negative maxima.
“Expected O(nk) time, O(k) auxiliary space”: Outgoing/incoming frequency updates reuse the active window instead of recounting all k shipments at each endpoint.
“Expected O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The active frequency map can contain k identifiers; excluding the scalar result does not exclude that map.
“Expected O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Zero counts are deleted, so identifiers outside the length-k window do not accumulate to n retained keys when k is smaller.
